FARRA:v3p251/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p251/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p251/r1.claim: Yaṣlawhā and yuṣlāhā are both valid readings with broad latitude.

FARRA:v3p251/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p251/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p251/r2.claim: He thought he would not return to God, but he certainly will; balā begins the affirmative answer before the statement that God sees him.
FARRA:v3p251/r2.anchor: وقوله عز وجل: إنه ظن أن لن يحور (14) بلى (15) . أن لن يعود إلينا إلى الآخرة. بلى ليحورن،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r2.claim: He thought he would never return or be raised; the correction says he will return, and his Lord watched him from creation onward.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r2.anchor: أن لن يرجع إلينا ولن يبعث ثم قال: {بلى} {بلى} أي: ليس كما ظن

BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.claim: Al-Inshiqāq continues the close of al-Muṭaffifīn: allies enjoy reward and enemies receive punishment because they denied resurrection and judgment before their Creator-King.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على آخر المطففين من أن الأولياء ينعمون والأعداء يعذبون ، لأنهم كانوا لا يقرون بالبعث ولا بالعرض على الملك الذي أوجدهم ورباهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r3.claim: Ḥāra can mean to return to one’s Lord, diminish, or perish; the denial echoes those who say life is only worldly and time destroys them.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r3.anchor: أي يرجع إلى ربه أو ينقص أو لهلك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r4.claim: Bala affirms that the denier will surely return humbled, diminished, and ruined.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r5.claim: God saw the condemned person at his first creation and knows all his deeds, so leaving him unaccountable would contradict wisdom, justice, and sovereignty.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r5.anchor: في إعادته كما كان في ابتدائه وفي جميع أعماله وأحواله التي لا يجوز في عدل عادل ترك الحساب عليها

NAHHAS:v5p185/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p185/r22.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p185/r22.claim: Indeed the person will return and be resurrected; God knew his deeds and destination, while he sinned boldly because he thought he would not be raised.
NAHHAS:v5p185/r22.anchor: أي بلى ليحورن وليبعثن أن ربه كان به بصيرا بعمله وبما يصير إليه لأنه كان يرتكب المعاصي مجترئا عليها إذ كان عنده أنه لا يبعث

ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r14.claim: Contrary to his assumption, the person will undergo reversal and return to God through death and resurrection, as the preceding verse says.
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r14.anchor: Burada إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًۭا فَمُلَٰقِيهِ buyurulduğu üzere mevt ve ba‘s ile Allah’a rücû‘dur.

ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r15.claim: God sees and watches all his deeds, so He will bring him back, reckon with him, and requite him.
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r15.anchor: Bütün yaptıklarını görüp gözetip duruyor. Binâen‘aleyh onu kaçırmaz, behemehâl çevirecek

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p245/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p245/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p245/r1.claim: God's watching over people refutes their denial of return: He will call them to Him, consistently with His power, wisdom, justice and mercy; this is used elsewhere as an argument for Judgment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p245/r1.anchor: The fact is that their Lord is watching over them

STUDYQURAN:84:15/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:84:15/r1.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:84:15/r1.claim: Nay means they will in fact return; God has observed all their actions from creation until resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:84:15/r1.anchor: God has been aware of all their actions from the moment He created them until the moment He resurrects them

TABATABAI:84:7-15/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:84:7-15/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:84:7-15/r11.claim: The reply rejects his expectation: he will return, and God sees his deeds, since He is his Lord, governs him, knows his actions, and assigns their recompense.
TABATABAI:84:7-15/r11.anchor: رد لظنه أي ليس الأمر كما ظنه بل يحور ويرجع

TABATABAI:84:7-15/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:84:7-15/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:84:7-15/r12.claim: God's lordship and full awareness, together with His charge to humans and the recompense due for their deeds, prove that they must return to Him.
TABATABAI:84:7-15/r12.anchor: وكان يحيط به علما ويرى ما كان من أعماله وقد كلفه بما كلف ولأعماله جزاء خيرا أو شرا فلا بد أن يرجع إليه

BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r14.claim: God sees the person and every deed that warrants recompense; divine wisdom therefore requires resurrection, accounting, and repayment rather than leaving deeds without consequence, warning all accountable people against sin.
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r14.anchor: بحيث لا تخفى منها خافية فلا بد من رجعه وحسابه وجزائه عليها حتما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل والفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r6.claim: Muqātil and al-Farrāʾ explain the answer “yes indeed” to mean that he will return and be resurrected.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r6.anchor: قال الله تعالى: {بلى} (¬5) ليحورن، وليبعثن. قاله مقاتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p362/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p362/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p362/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī says God saw him from the time He created him until He resurrected him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p362/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: بصيرا به من خلقه إلى أن بعثه (¬3) (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p362/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p362/r2.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p362/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says God saw what had been decreed for him in the Preserved Record: wretchedness and disgrace.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p362/r2.anchor: وقال عطاء: بصيرا بما سبق عليه في أم الكتاب من الشقاء والخزي (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p362/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p362/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p362/r3.claim: Muqātil explains this as God knowing when He will resurrect him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p362/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p362/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p362/r4.claim: Abū Isḥāq says God saw him before creating him and knew that he would return to Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p362/r4.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: كان به بصيرا قبل أن يخلقه، عالما بأن مرجعه إليه (¬8)

QASHANI:84:13-15/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:84:13-15/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:84:13-15/r2.claim: Indeed, he will return, and his Lord has seen him and will recompense him according to his state.
QASHANI:84:13-15/r2.anchor: { بلى } ليحورن { إن ربه كان به بصيرا } فيجازيه على حسب حاله

SAMIN-DURR:84:15/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:15/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:15/r1.claim: بلى answers the preceding negation in لن; إن introduces the answer to an implicit oath.
SAMIN-DURR:84:15/r1.anchor: جواب للنفي في " لن " ، و " إن " جواب قسم مقدر

ZAJJAJ:v5p304/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p304/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p304/r9.claim: God knew the person before creating him and knows that his return is to Him.
ZAJJAJ:v5p304/r9.anchor: قبل أن يخلقه، عالما بأن مرجعه إليه - عز وجل -

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r4.claim: بلى affirms the proposition after negation: he certainly will return.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r4.anchor: بلى: إيجاب بعد النفي، أي بلى ليحورن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r5.claim: God sees all his deeds, so he must return and be recompensed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r5.anchor: إن ربه كان به بصيرا: أي لا تخفى عليه أفعاله، فلا بد من حوره ومجازاته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r12.claim: Verses 7–15 detail the return to God: right-hand recipients are believers, those given the book behind their backs are polytheists, and the passage divides humanity by its outcome.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r12.anchor: هذا تفصيل الإجمال الذي في قوله : { إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا فملاقيه } ( الانشقاق : 6 ) أي رجوع جميع الناس أولئك إلى الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r2.claim: بلى cancels a negative assertion; it usually answers a negative question but can also follow a non-interrogative denial, as in 7:172 and 64:7.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r2.anchor: يجاب به الكلام المنفي لإبطال نفيه وأكثر وقوعه بعد الاستفهام عن النفي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r3.claim: Here بلى begins a new sentence, as answer particles do.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r4.claim: The clause explains بلى: the denier’s assumption is false because his Lord informed him through the Messenger that he will be resurrected.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r4.anchor: يعني أن ظنه باطل لأن ربه أنبأه بأنه يبعث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r5.claim: إن reinforces the rebuttal of his denial of the resurrection taught by the Messenger; God knows his state while he does not, as 2:216 says.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r5.anchor: لرده إنكاره البعث الذي أخبر الله به على لسان رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r6.claim: بصيرا takes ب because intransitive بصر means to see someone clearly; the preposition conveys attachment or contact.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r6.anchor: فالباء فيه معناها الملابسة أو الإلصاق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r7.claim: Resurrection enables recompense: God knows people’s deeds and their differing moral worth, so justice requires reward and punishment in an eternal life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r7.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى حكمة البعث للجزاء لأن رب الناس عليم بأحوالهم فمنهم المصلح ومنهم المفسد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r8.claim: Sight here is a metaphor for complete knowledge of a person’s state.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r8.anchor: وأطلق البصر هنا على العلم التام بالشيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r9.claim: The pronoun refers to the person who thought he would not return; God knows his circumstances, not merely his essence.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r10.claim: Preposing به emphasizes that God certainly knows him and also serves the verse endings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r10.anchor: أي بصير به لا محالة مع مراعاة الفواصل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r4.claim: God answers that the human will return and nothing is hidden from His sight, issuing a threat.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r4.anchor: ثم رد تعالى على ظن هذا الكافر بقوله: بلى، أي يحور ويرجع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p357#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p357#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p357#2/r7.claim: Indeed, God will resurrect him as He first created him and repay him for good and evil deeds, for God has always known him fully.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p357#2/r7.anchor: يعني: بلى سيعيده الله كما بدأه، ويجازيه على أعماله خيرها وشرها

JISHUMI:v10p7338/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7338/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v10p7338/r6.claim: One explanation contrasts the human’s belief that he will not return with God’s decisive statement that he will, since God sees him.
JISHUMI:v10p7338/r6.anchor: قيل: هو يخبر عن ظنه أن لن يحور، والله يخبر ويقطع أنه يحور، وهو بصير به.

JISHUMI:v10p7338/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7338/r7.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v10p7338/r7.claim: Another paraphrase says he will return to the afterlife; God knows his states and will recompense him appropriately.
JISHUMI:v10p7338/r7.anchor: وقيل: تقديره: بلى سيرجع إلى الآخرة، والله عالم بأحواله، سيجازيه بالمستحق.

JISHUMI:v10p7338/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7338/r8.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v10p7338/r8.claim: A third view says he returns to a Lord who has always seen him; without an afterlife, he would not have been charged with obligations.
JISHUMI:v10p7338/r8.anchor: وقيل: بل يحور إلى رب كان به بصيرا، ولو لم تكن الآخرة لما كلف.

JISHUMI:v10p7341/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7341/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7341/r1.claim: God knows the person’s states and deeds and will repay him for them.
JISHUMI:v10p7341/r1.anchor: (إن ربه كان به بصيرا) عالما بأحواله وأعماله فيجازيه عليها.

MUQATIL:84:10-15/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:84:10-15/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:84:10-15/r5.claim: His Lord is the One who created him and is witness to his deeds.
MUQATIL:84:10-15/r5.anchor: يقول: الذي خلقه { به بصيرا } [آية: 15] إنه شهيد لعمله

QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r1.claim: The Prophet sought refuge from al-ḥawr after al-kawr, a decline after increase; another transmission has “after al-kawn,” a dispersion after completion.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r1.anchor: اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الحور بعد الكور

QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r2.claim: The expression “ḥawr in a maḥārah” means one loss after another, used of a person's affairs declining.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r2.anchor: وفي المثل «حور في محارة» أي نقصان في نقصان. يضرب للرجل إذا كان أمره يدبر

QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r3.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r3.claim: A poet says that blame remains while the group's increase turns into decline, using ḥawr for deterioration.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر: واستعجلوا عن خفيف المضغ فازدردوا والذم يبقى وزاد القوم في حور

QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r4.claim: Aḥāra can mean to return something: a mill that produces no flour “has not returned anything.” Al-hawr can also mean destruction.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r4.anchor: والحور أيضا: الاسم من قولك: طحنت الطاحنة فما أحارت شيئا أي ما ردت شيئا من الدقيق

QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r5.claim: Abu Ubayd explains the rajaz line's “well with no ḥawr” as a well of destruction, with lā treated as extra.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r5.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: أي بئر حور، و «لا» زائدة

QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r6.speaker: معمر وعبد الرزاق
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r6.claim: A variant “after al-kawn” means after affairs have spread out following completion; Ma'mar says the expression is al-kunti, a good person who changes into a bad one.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r6.anchor: وروي «بعد الكون» ومعناه من انتشار الأمر بعد تمامه. وسئل معمر عن الحور بعد الكون، فقال: هو الكنتي

QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r7.claim: Abu Amr says kunti describes an old man who says “I was so in my youth”; a poet's “I became a kunti” illustrates it.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r7.anchor: قال أبو عمرو: يقال للرجل إذا شاخ: كنتي، كأنه نسب إلى قوله: كنت في شبابي كذا. قال: فأصبحت كنتيا

QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r8.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r8.claim: Ibn al-A'rabi says a kunti boasts “I was young” or “I was brave,” while a kāni says he once had wealth or horses and used to give or ride.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r8.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: الكنتي: هو الذي يقول: كنت شابا، وكنت شجاعا، والكاني هو الذي يقول: كان لي مال

QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r9.claim: Balā rejects the assumption of no return: the person will indeed return to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r9.anchor: قوله تعالى: { بلى } أي ليس الأمر كما ظن، بل يحور إلينا ويرجع

QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r10.claim: God saw him before creating him and knew that his return would be to Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r10.anchor: { إن ربه كان به بصيرا } قبل أن يخلقه، عالما بأن مرجعه إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r11.claim: Another parsing makes “balā” affirm that he will return, then starts a new sentence: his Lord has seen him from creation until resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r11.anchor: وقيل: بلى ليحورن وليرجعن. ثم استأنف فقال: «إن ربه كان به بصيرا» من يوم خلقه إلى أن بعثه

QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r12.claim: Another explanation is that God knows what was decreed for the person, whether wretchedness or felicity.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:15/r12.anchor: وقيل: عالما بما سبق له من الشقاء والسعادة
